beats.title: Council of Nicaea Meets
beats.description: Bishops gathered by the Roman emperor at a city in Asia Minor and drew up a creed that still anchors Christian belief.

beats.title: Leo I Meets Attila
beats.description: A pope rode out to meet the Hun king near Mantua, and Attila turned back from his invasion of Italy.

beats.title: Gregory the Great Is Elected
beats.description: A Roman aristocrat turned monk became pope amid plague and flood, and went on to shape the medieval papacy.

beats.title: Pope Stephen II Crosses the Alps
beats.description: A pope travelled to the Frankish king to seek protection, and the gift that followed gave the papacy lands of its own.

beats.title: Leo III Crowns Charlemagne
beats.description: On Christmas Day in St Peter's, the pope placed a crown on the Frankish king and hailed him as emperor of the Romans.

beats.title: East and West Split
beats.description: Papal legates and the patriarch of Constantinople excommunicated each other, a rift between Rome and the Orthodox East that never healed.

beats.title: Cardinals Win the Right to Elect
beats.description: A Roman synod decreed that the cardinals would choose future popes, shutting out emperors and city nobles.

beats.title: Henry IV Humbles Himself at Canossa
beats.description: An excommunicated emperor stood barefoot in the snow for days to beg forgiveness from the pope.

beats.title: Concordat of Worms
beats.description: Pope and emperor agreed that the Church would invest bishops with spiritual authority while the ruler granted their lands.

beats.title: Fourth Lateran Council
beats.description: Innocent III gathered hundreds of bishops in Rome to set doctrine on the Eucharist and require yearly confession.

beats.title: The Longest Conclave Begins
beats.description: Cardinals at Viterbo failed to agree for years, until locals locked them in, cut their food and removed the roof.
beats.note: Began 1268 (sources say Nov or Dec); Gregory X chosen 1271

beats.title: Celestine V Resigns
beats.description: A hermit elected pope after a two-year deadlock gave up the office within months, a rare papal abdication.

beats.title: Boniface VIII Opens First Jubilee
beats.description: Pilgrims flocked to Rome after the pope promised special forgiveness to those who visited its basilicas.

beats.title: The Papacy Moves to Avignon
beats.description: A French pope settled in a town on the Rhone, beginning decades in which the popes lived outside Rome.

beats.title: The Western Schism Begins
beats.description: Cardinals elected a second pope against the one they had just chosen, leaving Christendom with rival popes.

beats.title: Constance Ends the Schism
beats.description: A council deposed or accepted the rival claimants and elected Martin V, reuniting the Western Church under one pope.

beats.title: Rodrigo Borgia Becomes Alexander VI
beats.description: A Spanish cardinal reputedly bought his way to the papal throne and went on to rule as the most notorious Renaissance pope.

beats.title: Julius II Begins New St Peter's
beats.description: The warrior pope laid the first stone of a vast new basilica to replace the ancient church over Peter's tomb.

beats.title: Michelangelo Paints Sistine Ceiling
beats.description: A pope pressed a reluctant sculptor into painting the chapel vault, producing scenes from Genesis.

beats.title: Leo X Excommunicates Luther
beats.description: A papal bull cast out the German monk whose challenge to indulgences had split Western Christianity.

beats.title: England Rejects the Pope
beats.description: Parliament declared the king supreme head of the Church in England after Rome refused to annul his marriage.

beats.title: The Council of Trent Opens
beats.description: Bishops met in a northern Italian city to answer the Protestant challenge and reform Catholic teaching and discipline.

beats.title: Gregory XIII Reforms the Calendar
beats.description: A papal bull dropped ten days and refined leap years, giving the world the calendar still in common use.

beats.title: Galileo Is Tried by the Inquisition
beats.description: Under Urban VIII, the Roman Inquisition forced an elderly astronomer to renounce his claim that the Earth moves.

beats.title: Clement XIV Suppresses the Jesuits
beats.description: Under pressure from Catholic monarchs, the pope dissolved the Society of Jesus across the world.

beats.title: Revolutionary France Seizes Rome
beats.description: French troops proclaimed a Roman republic and carried the aged Pius VI off into captivity.

beats.title: Pius VII at Napoleon's Coronation
beats.description: The pope travelled to Paris, only to watch the emperor take the crown from the altar and place it on his own head.

beats.title: Pius IX Elected
beats.description: A reform-minded cardinal became pope and went on to hold the office longer than anyone in history apart from Peter.

beats.title: Papal Infallibility Declared
beats.description: The First Vatican Council defined that the pope cannot err when he teaches on faith and morals from his chair.

beats.title: Rerum Novarum on Workers
beats.description: Leo XIII issued a landmark letter on the rights of labour and the duties of employers, founding modern Catholic social teaching.

beats.title: The Lateran Treaty
beats.description: Italy and the Holy See agreed terms that created the independent state of Vatican City.

beats.title: Pius XII Defines the Assumption
beats.description: A pope used his infallible authority, rarely invoked, to declare Mary's assumption into heaven a dogma.

beats.title: John XXIII Opens Vatican II
beats.description: A surprise council brought thousands of bishops to Rome to modernise the Church, later allowing Mass in local languages.

beats.title: A Polish Pope Is Elected
beats.description: After a pope's death within weeks of his election, cardinals chose the first non-Italian pope in centuries.

beats.title: John Paul II Visits Poland
beats.description: Crowds of millions greeted the pope in his homeland, a visit credited with emboldening opposition to communist rule.

beats.title: Pope Shot in St Peter's Square
beats.description: A gunman wounded John Paul II as he greeted pilgrims, and the pope later forgave him in prison.

beats.title: Vatican Clears Galileo
beats.description: John Paul II formally acknowledged that the Church had erred in condemning the astronomer centuries earlier.

beats.title: John Paul II Asks Forgiveness
beats.description: During a jubilee Mass, the pope publicly apologised for sins committed by members of the Church over the centuries.

beats.title: Benedict XVI Is Elected
beats.description: White smoke rose over the Sistine Chapel as a German cardinal succeeded the long-serving Polish pope.

beats.title: First Latin American Pope Elected
beats.description: A cardinal from Argentina was chosen days after the pope's resignation, the first modern pope to step down.
beats.note: Benedict resigned and Francis was elected in 2013

beats.title: First American Pope Elected
beats.description: A cardinal from Chicago was elected after the death of Francis, the first pope born in the United States.
